findings.issue: The note says more than its two read sources show. Pinkerton (660-663) says the Kyiv academy was founded 'after the manner of the Polish schools'. He does not say Jesuit colleges. Pinkerton writes in 1814 and Golubev in 1883, so neither speaks for 'historians' today. Golubev (18351-18355) says that the outer polish of scholastic learning, rhetorical phrases and clever speech, proper to Western and above all Jesuit colleges, at once ('сразу же') took deep root in the Mohyla college. 'Came straight from Western colleges' turns 'at once took root' into a claim about direct origin.
findings.fix: A memoir printed in 1814 says the Kyiv academy was set up after the manner of the Polish schools, and Latin became its main language. In 1883 the historian Stefan Golubev wrote about the college. He said the showy learning and clever speech of Western colleges, the Jesuit ones above all, took deep root there at once. (FRE 62.1, FK 9.2; grade, type and sources unchanged)
